title: Transfer
text: Viele Planungsaufgaben in der Praxis sind zu komplex für Tabellenkalkulation und Erfahrungswissen allein: Dienstpläne, Bettenbelegung, Lager, Touren, Verladung. Hinzu kommt Unsicherheit – Nachfrage, Patientenaufkommen oder Ausfälle sind nicht genau vorhersehbar. Genau hier setzt meine Arbeit an: Ich verbinde mathematische Optimierung, Machine Learning und Simulation zu Entscheidungsunterstützung, die in realen Prozessen funktioniert.

title: Transfer
text:
Typische Fragestellungen


 Gesundheitswesen
Wie viele Intensivbetten werden morgen gebraucht? Wie lassen sich Aufnahmen, Behandlungspfade und Dienstpläne so planen, dass Engpässe seltener werden?


 Personaleinsatzplanung
Schicht- und Dienstpläne, die Bedarf, Regeln und Wünsche berücksichtigen – und robust bleiben, wenn der Bedarf schwankt.


 Logistik und Handel
Lagerplatzzuordnung, Bestellpolitiken für verderbliche Ware, Verlade- und Tourenplanung.


 Optimierung per Sprache
Im Projekt OptimizationChat untersuchen wir, wie große Sprachmodelle helfen, Planungsprobleme aus der Industrie zu formulieren und zu lösen.

title: Research
text: My research sits at the intersection of Operations Research and Machine Learning. I develop decision support methods for planning problems in which uncertainty matters, and apply them in health care, logistics and environmental decision-making. A common methodological thread is the use of structured models, such as networks and decision diagrams, that are expressive enough for real-world problems and at the same time amenable to learning. Many papers belong to more than one of the lines below; papers are listed newest first. For funded projects, see Projects.

title: Research
text:
Decisions under uncertainty
Many planning decisions have to be made before demand, arrivals or durations are known. I work on two-stage, robust and data-driven approaches that account for this uncertainty, on quantifying the value of information, and on decision-focused learning, where predictive models are trained with respect to the decisions they inform.

title: Research
text:
Network models and decision diagrams
State-expanded networks encode complex rules, for example for shifts and rosters, in the structure of a graph, so that the remaining optimization model stays simple. Decision diagrams provide relaxations and bounds for discrete optimization. My work develops such models and uses machine learning to make them smaller and their bounds stronger.

title: Research
text:
Health care analytics
Hospitals have to plan beds, staff and treatments while patient arrivals and lengths of stay are uncertain. Together with hospital partners and colleagues from medicine, I develop simulation-, learning- and optimization-based decision support for such problems: forecasting and managing intensive care occupancy, scheduling ICU admissions, scheduling clinical pathways, and rostering staff. I have also worked with clinicians and computer scientists on algorithm-based rehabilitation after cochlear implantation.

title: Research
text:
Language models for optimization
Formulating an optimization model is often the bottleneck for using optimization in practice. In the project OptimizationChat we investigate how large language models can help to formalize and solve industrial planning problems through natural-language interaction. Related work uses language models to discover heuristics for combinatorial optimization.


Hottung, Berto, Hua, …, Römer, …, Tierney (2026). VRPAgent: LLM-Driven Discovery of Heuristic Operators for Vehicle Routing Problems. Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR). arXiv

title: Research
text:
Environment and sustainability
Environmental decisions, such as where to monitor, what to protect and how to weigh ecological against economic goals, are made under substantial uncertainty and with limited budgets. Together with environmental economists and marine biodiversity researchers, I study the value of information in environmental monitoring, trade-off analysis for environmental decisions, and, in a DFG project, decision-focused learning for planning marine protected areas.

title: Research
text:
Logistics and supply chains
Many of my projects start from operational problems in logistics and retail: service network design, inventory routing, storage assignment and inventory management in e-grocery fulfilment, truck loading, and most recently large-scale supply network optimization in the automotive industry. Logistics also extends into space: a time-space network approach for delivery scheduling won first place in the “Delivery Scheduling” category of the ESA/GECCO Space Optimisation Competition 2022, and our exact framework for the space-time dependent TSP (INFORMS Journal on Computing) solves asteroid routing problems, in which a spacecraft visits a sequence of asteroids (Space.com).

title: Projects
text:
2025–2028 · European Regional Development Fund (EFRE), Industrie.IN.NRW
Mathematische Optimierung auf Basis natürlichsprachlicher Interaktion: Industrierelevante Probleme formalisieren und lösen. Turning a real planning problem into an optimization model usually requires an expert dialogue between practitioners and modelers. OptimizationChat investigates how large language models can support and partly automate this dialogue, so that industrial planning problems can be formalized and solved through natural-language interaction. Joint project with Fraunhofer IOSB-INA and more than ten regional companies; I lead the Bielefeld sub-project.
Project page




2024–2027 · German Research Foundation (DFG), project no. 540478491
Planning marine protected areas requires predictions, for example of species distributions, that feed into an optimization model. Instead of training these predictions for accuracy alone, the project trains them for the quality of the resulting protection decisions. The approach embeds learned models into a heuristic solution procedure and tunes both jointly, without requiring derivatives, and can handle uncertainty in constraints as well as in the objective. Principal investigator, jointly with Kevin Tierney.
GEPRIS

title: Projects
text:
Completed projects

Combining Graphical Optimization Models and Machine Learning for Planning and Scheduling under Uncertainty
2019–2025 · NRW Return Programme (Rückkehrprogramm) of the State of North Rhine-Westphalia
The NRW Return Programme supports researchers returning from abroad in building their own independent research group in North Rhine-Westphalia. This grant funded the establishment of my Decision Analytics group at Bielefeld University. The project combines graphical optimization models (state-expanded networks and decision diagrams) with machine learning to solve planning and scheduling problems under uncertainty. It laid the foundation for most of my current research lines, from learning-enhanced network models and decision diagram bounds to data-driven shift scheduling and decision support in health care. Sole principal investigator.
Network models and decision diagrams Decisions under uncertainty



An AI-based System for the Rehabilitation of Cochlear Implant Patients
2020–2022 · Anschubfonds Medizinische Forschung, Bielefeld University
Interdisciplinary project with Franz Kummert, Ingo Todt and Christoph Kayser on algorithm-based hearing and speech therapy after cochlear implantation; I led one of the sub-projects.
Publication in Brain Sciences



Generic and Efficient Personnel Scheduling Approaches Based on State-Expanded Network Formulations
2018–2019 · DFG research fellowship, project no. 398911053 · University of Toronto
A general method for building state-expanded network models for personnel scheduling, framed as dynamic programming, together with exact and heuristic techniques to keep the networks small. The project also led to new work on decision diagrams.
